blocks.text: If you're feeding a family near Bondi and the bill keeps making you wince, here's the good news: yes, kids really can eat free across Sydney's Eastern Suburbs, most often on a quiet weeknight when one free children's meal comes with each adult main. From Double Bay to Coogee there's a solid dozen pubs and clubs running some version of the deal — the catch is the exact night, time and fine print change often, so the most useful thing I can tell you is to confirm the current terms with the venue before you pile everyone in the car.

I've watched these offers come and go for years as a local parent, and the pattern is remarkably consistent even when the details aren't. Here's how the deals work, the venues worth checking, and the traps that catch families out.
How kids-eat-free deals usually work here
Almost every Eastern Suburbs offer follows the same shape, which makes them easy to plan around. The specifics vary by venue, but the structure rarely does.

items: One free kids' meal per adult main purchased — so two adults ordering means two free kids' meals
Children roughly 12 and under, ordering from a dedicated kids' menu (not the full à la carte list)
Dine-in only, and usually a set weeknight or a Sunday rather than every day
Some venues are members-only or need a quick sign-up at the door
School holidays are frequently excluded — the deals fill quiet trading nights

blocks.title: Always ring ahead — these change constantly
blocks.text: Kids-eat-free nights are among the most volatile things a pub markets. Nights get moved, offers get paused over holidays, and some quietly disappear. Treat any specific day or time you read online (including here) as a prompt to check the venue's own website, not a guarantee.

These are real, well-established family spots across the Eastern Suburbs. I'm deliberately not printing a night against each one, because that's the detail that drifts — click through to each venue to see what's on right now.

items: Easts (Bondi Junction) — big family bistro and the easiest bet a short bus or walk from the beach
Bondi Trattoria, Campbell Parade — a beachfront Italian institution that's long looked after families
The Clovelly Hotel — a relaxed pub an easy hop down the coast, popular with local parents
The Golden Sheaf, Double Bay — the standout, with a genuine Sunday kids-eat-free offer
Watsons Bay Hotel — Sunday sessions with harbour sunsets and a family-friendly setup
Coogee Pavilion — a Merivale mega-venue with a dedicated kids' playroom upstairs
Matraville Hotel and other local leagues and bowling clubs, which regularly run family nights

blocks.text: The one deal I'd bank on is The Golden Sheaf in Double Bay: kids eat free all day every Sunday with the purchase of any adult main, and during school holidays they stack it with a free kids' activity program (think face-painting and craft). Get there early on a sunny Sunday — the beer garden fills fast. Confirm the current details on the Sheaf's own Kids Eat Free page before you go.
Getting the most out of the deal

A few habits save my family real money and stress. Book a table where you can — free-kids nights get busy. Ask at ordering whether the offer needs membership or a minimum adult spend, as that's the usual small print. And if you're going in the holidays, double-check it's still running that week, since that's when venues most often pull it.
My honest take: pick one reliable local, get to know its family night, and you'll eat out with the kids far more often than you'd think — without the end-of-month bill shock.

items.q: Where do kids actually eat free near Bondi Beach?
items.a: The closest options are the big family bistros just inland and along the coast — Easts at Bondi Junction, Bondi Trattoria on Campbell Parade and The Clovelly Hotel. For a confirmed offer, The Golden Sheaf in Double Bay runs kids-eat-free every Sunday. Check each venue's current deal before you go.

items.q: What day is the Golden Sheaf kids-eat-free deal?
items.a: Every Sunday, all day, with any adult main meal, and during school holidays it comes with a free kids' activity program. It's the most dependable Eastern Suburbs offer I know of — confirm the current terms on the Sheaf's website.

items.q: Is there usually an age limit?
items.a: Yes — most kids-eat-free deals apply to children around 12 and under, ordering from a set kids' menu rather than the main menu. The exact age cut-off varies by venue, so ask when you book.

items.q: Do kids-eat-free deals run during school holidays?
items.a: Often not. Because these offers exist to fill quiet trading nights, many venues pause or exclude them over the holidays. If you're planning a holiday outing, ring ahead to check that week specifically.

items.q: Do I need to be a member?
items.a: Sometimes. A handful of clubs limit the deal to members, though sign-up is usually free or a token few dollars at the door. Others have no membership requirement — it's worth asking when you order so there are no surprises on the bill.

blocks.text: Bottom line: feeding kids out in the Eastern Suburbs doesn't have to be expensive. There's a genuine spread of free-kids nights from Double Bay to Coogee — just treat the specific night as something to confirm, not assume.
